transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Jun Park (Redwood SE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Priya Anand (MeridianAI Head of MLOps), Tom Rivers (MeridianAI SRE), Olga Petrov (MeridianAI Security), Marco Li (MeridianAI Platform)

Auto-generated summary: Quick workshop to show provenance and replay, collect logs for POC.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, and we'll do a console lab focused on provenance and replay, Jun's gonna drive most of the demo. Can everyone hear me okay?
[00:12] Priya: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks. We have about an hour, excited to see the replay stuff — we've had trouble reproducing intermittent latencies.
[00:22] Jun: Great. Quick agenda: trace correlation, request inspector, timeline playback, then KV cache eviction scenarios and fallback behavior, and finally security/compliance Qs.
[00:35] Tom: We get those bursts where tokens slow down, and sometimes the model switches mid-request to a smaller variant, not sure why — we think it might be fallback but need proof.
[00:48] Jun: Yep. We'll show how the console labels fallbacks, and how you can reconstruct the path — provenance shows which routing policy fired and why. Note: small audio drop there, apologies if you missed a word.
[00:58] [Screen share starts] Jun: I'm in the Console now. Top right you can see the Request Inspector — filter by correlation id or user id. I'm going to load a sample request from a high-latency trace.
[01:15] Jun: Here is the timeline view, you can see token-by-token timings, and a spike at 1.2s per token. The trace has annotations for batching events and kernel selection.
[01:30] Priya: That token spike, is that measured on the GPU side or queueing? We currently can't tell if it's our network or the infer node.
[01:40] Jun: Good q. The console shows pipeline events: routing, queue wait, kernel execution. In this trace the queue wait jumped — looks like autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough. You'll see a 'queueWait' span here.
[01:56] Sofia: Also check the model variant tag — we surface the variant name and quantization profile, sometimes fallback happens when memory is low and we choose a quantized variant.
[02:10] Tom: That's what we suspected, but we saw model mismatch in logs and worried about degraded output. How do you prove the fallback reason?
[02:20] Jun: In the provenance pane we show the decision stack: policy name, available variants, mem usage threshold, and the observed metric that triggered it. I'll expand it.
[02:36] [Jun clicks] Jun: See here — 'fallback_policy_v2' fired because memAvailable < 1.2GB. The request then routed to 'redwood-mini-q4'. The transcript sometimes mislabels the model name as 'mini-q'.
[02:50] Priya: MemAvailable — that's host-level GPU memory? Or container?
[02:58] Jun: It's per-inference-pod available memory aggregated by the runtime. We note the metric with a timestamp so you get exact correlation.
[03:10] Marco: Can we export that provenance as JSON to attach to our incident ticketing?
[03:16] Jun: Yes, use the 'Export trace' button — it gives JSON with spans, env labels, and a small binary KV snapshot pointer. We'll attach an export to a ticket.
[03:28] Sofia: We'll share the export guide in the follow-up. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/replay-export (shared)
[03:36] Priya: Good. Show us the partial replay — we only want to replay the tail end, not the whole day.
[03:44] Jun: Right — 'partial playback' allows you to select time windows and subset of requests by filter. I'll replay the last 15 minutes of this request group. Starting playback...
[04:00] [Playback starts] Jun: The console spins up a temporary replay environment; note this is isolated and uses pinned model variants unless you opt to route to production.
[04:12] Tom: That isolates cost and risk, good. During replay, can we inject synthetic load? We want to recreate the burst.
[04:21] Jun: You can. There's an 'inject' tab — you can replay with increased concurrency to see queueing behavior. I'll bump concurrency to 7.
[04:35] [Playback shows queue growth] Jun: See the queueWait increases and then fallback policy triggers earlier because mem pressure is reached faster. The console annotates the exact span where a fallback occurred.
[04:48] Priya: Any chance playback uses cached KV to give false results? Our live runs use per-user KV and sometimes the cache avoids hitting model.
[04:58] Jun: Important point — the replay has three modes: 'use live cache snapshot', 'fresh run', or 'use supplied KV snapshot'. If you choose 'use live cache snapshot' you may see less load. For tests we used 'fresh run' to force misses.
[05:14] Marco: How do we capture KV snapshots?
[05:18] Jun: There is an export that includes KV pointers; you can capture a snapshot at time T. We'll demo this later in the lab.
[05:26] [Short pause while Jun prepares a different request]
[05:40] [00:05:40] Ravi: Quick note — when you look at the request inspector notice the correlation header name is sometimes X-Req-Id vs X-Corr-Id, so you might need multiple filters.
[05:52] Priya: Ah we use x-req-id across services, thanks.
[05:55] Jun: Ok loading a second trace that includes an error: 'inference_timeout' and a fallback.
[06:04] [06:04] Jun: You can see stack trace of where the runtime timed out waiting for KV filling — the console surfaces 'kvFetchTimeout' span. Sometimes transcribers show 'KV cash' which is wrong but you know what it means.
[06:20] Olga: From a security perspective we need to know what is in these exports — do they contain user PII or prompt contents? Our security team insists on redaction.
[06:30] Jun: Good call. Export settings allow redaction of prompt text and scrub PII fields. We also support on-prem export where exports are stored into your S3 behind VPC endpoints.
[06:42] Olga: Do you integrate with KMS? We need HSM-backed encryption.
[06:47] Jun: Yes — KMS/HSM integrations supported, we log key usage in audit logs. We'll include the SOC2 control mapping in the follow-up pack.
[06:58] Sofia: We'll attach our compliance checklist and the private deploy package.
[07:06] [07:06] Tom: Back to the error — how can we tell if the slowdown was caused by serialization in our middleware vs Redwood runtime?
[07:15] Jun: Correlation again. The timeline has ingress span (your middleware), network, queue wait, and kernel exec. If the ingress span dominates, it's on your side. In this trace the ingress was negligible.
[07:27] Priya: I see a long ingress for one request earlier — likely retries from our side. Could misconfigured client-side retry be contributing.
[07:36] Sofia: We can show retry detectors as an anomaly signal in Optimize. It surfaces bursty retry loops that spike costs.
[07:44] Priya: Nice. Can Optimize also recommend batching and quantization options?
[07:50] Jun: Yes, Optimize suggests batching windows and quantization profiles per workload. But for this replay we focused on runtime behavior.
[07:58] [08:00] Jun: Now walking through a KV cache eviction scenario: I'm going to set a synthetic workload that forces the KV to evict the large user state.
[08:10] [Synth load applied] Jun: Eviction occurs; you can see 'kvEvict' spans and the following requests show misses with higher latencies. The console links the eviction event to a GC and a memory pressure metric.
[08:26] Marco: When eviction happens, do you automatically route to a fallback model or just run with additional latency?
[08:33] Jun: Configurable policy: conservative mode will wait and retry, aggressive mode falls back to smaller model variant. We show the policy decision and time-of-decision in the trace.
[08:44] Priya: Is fallback deterministic? We need reproducible behavior for SLO testing.
[08:50] Jun: Deterministic given the same metric thresholds and resource snapshot. But if autoscaling changes capacity mid-replay you can see different outcomes — the console's 'versioned run' pins capacity and model variants to make replays deterministic.
[09:02] Tom: How do we pin capacity in POC?
[09:06] Jun: Use 'Replay Varying' vs 'Replay Pinned' toggle — pinned mode reserves a test pool. We'll show cost and ephemeral pool options.
[09:16] [09:16] Sofia: Quick interjection — Marco, when you send logs, include the cluster metrics and the request headers, that helps us match spans.
[09:28] Marco: Will do.
[09:30] Priya: On redaction — if we redact prompts, does that remove ability to detect prompt-sensitive failures?
[09:38] Jun: It reduces fidelity. We recommend a redaction policy that retains token length and token-level deltas but removes PII content; that still lets you spot KV misses or model truncation issues.
[09:52] Olga: Any notes on retention of exports for audits?
[09:56] Jun: Retention is configurable on your account; exports stored in your S3 can be held per your retention policy. Audit logs are available for 90 days by default; extended retention is an add-on.
[10:08] [10:08] Jun: Now demoing a model-regression detection — the console links quality regressions to specific rollouts. You can replay a set of prompts against version A vs B and get delta metrics.
[10:22] Priya: Can that run at scale? We have 10k daily regression prompts.
[10:27] Jun: Yes, there's a batch eval runner. We'll include the runner template.
[10:34] [10:34] Sofia: We often get this question: how to correlate debug traces with billing spikes? The Console cross-links cost per-token with per-request traces.
[10:44] Tom: That cross-link would help explain a sudden monthly bill spike.
[10:47] Jun: Right — there's a cost breakdown pane on each trace.
[10:52] [11:00] [Demo continues: Jun flips to an incident deck] Jun: Here's an incident playbook: step 1 collect traces & exports, step 2 run a partial replay with pinned capacity, step 3 verify quality delta and rollback if needed.
[11:16] Priya: If we need a rollback, can Redwood automatically route new traffic to previous model until we patch?
[11:22] Jun: Yes, automated rollback or canary with percentage routing. It's in the console under Rollouts.
[11:30] Sofia: Ok quick poll — are there any blockers from security or procurement to starting a small POC?
[11:38] Olga: Procurement wants the enterprise terms and an NDA, security wants SOC2 artifact and KMS details. Also network diagrams for VPC peering.
[11:48] Sofia: We'll include the enterprise agreement, SOC2, and network diagrams. I'll tag our solutions architect on the email.
[11:55] Priya: Great. For the POC scope — we want KV eviction and fallback reproducibility, plus 1h throughput baseline. That ok?
[12:04] Jun: Totally. We'll run baseline at X qps and then run a spike to trigger fallback. We'll collect the traces and provide a replay report.
[12:14] Marco: Any rate limits that might affect our playback?
[12:18] Jun: The replay infra uses separate quota and can be configured to higher limits for POC. We'll request quota bump for your account during the POC window.
[12:28] [12:28] Sofia: Ok last section — quick navigation tips: request inspector filters, timeline heatmaps, the event-search box supports regex, and the playback console has step-through mode which is handy.
[12:44] Tom: The step-through will help our SREs.
[12:48] [12:48] Jun: Wrapping up demo. We recorded the session and will attach the short Looms for trace export and KV demo.
[12:57] Priya: Thanks, that was useful. One ask — can Jun produce the KV eviction demo as a short recorded script so we can run it ourselves?
[13:06] Jun: Yes, that's in the action items.
[13:10] Olga: On compliance — also share your FedRAMP gap analysis if any.
[13:16] Sofia: We'll check and share what we have; some regions may require extra controls.
[13:22] [13:22] Sofia: Quick recap and next steps: we'll share export guide + Loom, Jun will craft the KV eviction reproducible demo, customer to send logs and cluster metrics, Redwood to prepare POC kickoff invite and quota request.
[13:36] Priya: Sounds good.
[13:39] Tom: Thank you.
[13:41] Sofia: Thanks all — we'll follow up by EOD with the packet.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (KV cash), speaker labels sometimes coarse. References shared: replay-export guide (https://console.redwood.ai/docs/replay-export), compliance pack (link to be provided), benchmark workbook (shared on follow-up).

Explicit next steps captured in Action Items above.
